note:
Frozen split assignment. A case NEVER changes tranche: membership that moves after a tranche has been read silently contaminates the held-out set.

2026-08-23: re-stratified from scratch for the 0.0.1 baseline reset, discarding the prior manifest. This is the one deliberate breach of the rule above and it is behind gen-request-plan-cases.py --restratify.

READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING A TEST NUMBER: re-stratifying does not make the cases unread. Every case in 0.0.1 predates the reset and most were examined under the versions whose results the reset deleted, so `test` here is NOMINAL, not held-out. It buys stratified balance across grounding, nothing more. A genuinely unseen tranche needs genuinely new cases, written after this manifest and pinned to test before any capture reads them -- which is what the 97-121 tranche did, and what its successor must do again.

Retired ids leave gaps here. Ids are positional in gen-request-plan-cases.py, so the retired slots stay open rather than renumbering every later case.

2026-08-26: ids 122-167 appended after the 0.2.0 rule change. They were written against a tree whose registry no longer makes them a lookup, and pinned here BEFORE any capture read them, so whatever landed in `test` is genuinely held out. Appended by hand, not by --restratify: re-stratifying would have moved every earlier case.

2026-08-30: ids 168-212 appended as batch 5, by hand and on the same terms as batch 4. This was the tranche `held_out_from` named while it lasted, and 122-167 was already not: the 0.2.0 labelling pass read all 18 of batch 4's `test` cases, which is why the 0.3.0 cut was taken with --held-out-from 168 (evals/labels/request-plan-0.3.0-sample.json). That cut spent batch 5 in turn, so BOTH ranges are now read and neither may be quoted as held out.

2026-09-05: ids 213-270 appended as batch 6, by hand and on the same terms as batches 4 and 5. Sized at 58 from the full 26-case `adjacent` analysis rather than from a fresh bet: batch 5's `adjacent` cases all grounded on capability-registry.sh EXCLUSIONS, which turns an adjacency test into a search test, so its 50% says nothing about the cell -- see the batch 6 entry in skills/request-plan/evals/evals.json's grading field. 23 of the 58 stratify to `test` (12 buried / 7 adjacent / 4 absent; 19 plan / 4 clarify). This tranche REPLACES batch 5's, which the 0.3.0 labelling pass spent in full.

`held_out_from` is the floor every consumer reads instead of hardcoding one: the first id of the newest tranche pinned before any capture read it. IT IS PINNED HERE TO 213, the first id of batch 6, in the same edit that appended batch 6 -- the key exists only while an unread tranche does, and the edit that spends a tranche is the edit that deletes it. Not 168, which names the tranche the 0.3.0 pass spent in full. The next capture to label every `test` case at or above 213 is the edit that must delete this key again, or re-point it at batch 7. A floor left naming a spent tranche would report a rate over already-labelled cases at a sampling fraction of 1.0, which label-align.py divides back out and nothing downstream could detect. --restratify writes neither this paragraph nor the key, for the same reason -- a full reshuffle leaves nothing held out.
